court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals

issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction and timeliness
issues.why: The court must confirm it has jurisdiction and that the notice of appeal and claims are properly before it.

issues.label: Standard of review per claim
issues.why: The court must select the correct review standard (de novo, abuse of discretion, clear error, sufficiency, plain error) for each issue.

issues.label: Issue preservation/waiver/forfeiture
issues.why: The court must determine whether objections were made at trial and the effect on review (plain error if not preserved).

issues.label: Harmless error vs prejudice
issues.why: For any error, the court must decide whether it was harmless beyond a reasonable doubt or substantially affected the verdict, depending on the right implicated.

issues.label: Cumulative error doctrine
issues.why: Even if individual errors are harmless, their combined effect may warrant reversal.

issues.label: Sufficiency standard (Jackson/Curley)
issues.why: The court must view evidence in the light most favorable to the verdict and decide whether a rational juror could convict.

issues.label: Identity evidence sufficiency
issues.why: Because the defense disputes the shooter’s identity, the court must assess whether identification proof was adequate.

issues.label: Photo array suggestiveness
issues.why: If challenged, the court must decide whether the lineup procedures were impermissibly suggestive and, if so, whether identification was nonetheless reliable.

issues.label: In-court ID admissibility
issues.why: If pretrial ID is tainted, the court must decide whether an independent basis supports in-court identification.

issues.label: Reliability factors for eyewitness ID
issues.why: The court must evaluate opportunity to view, attention, accuracy, certainty, and time lapse for Nance’s identification.

issues.label: Cross-racial identification concerns
issues.why: If applicable/raised, the court must consider whether special reliability concerns or instructions are required.

issues.label: Jury instructions on identification
issues.why: The court must determine whether the jury was properly instructed on assessing eyewitness identification.

issues.label: Surveillance video authentication
issues.why: The court must ensure the video was properly authenticated and admitted under evidence rules.

issues.label: Video relevance and Rule 403
issues.why: The court must balance probative value of video against unfair prejudice/confusion.

issues.label: Dealership records foundation
issues.why: The court must determine whether service records were properly admitted (business records, hearsay exceptions, foundation).

issues.label: Hearsay from dealership witness
issues.why: The court must decide whether any statements by others at the dealership were admitted for truth and, if so, whether an exception applies.

issues.label: Lay vs expert identification of car
issues.why: The court must decide if Johnson’s identification of the Maserati was permissible lay opinion or required expert qualification.

issues.label: Admissibility of customization features
issues.why: The court must determine if testimony about rims/tow-hook plate mount is relevant and not unduly speculative.

issues.label: Other-acts evidence (rim change request)
issues.why: Davis’s post-incident request to change rim color may be treated as consciousness-of-guilt and must satisfy non-propensity and Rule 403 limits.

issues.label: Consciousness-of-guilt evidence (flight)
issues.why: The court must decide whether evidence of leaving for Costa Rica/supporting evasive conduct is admissible and whether flight instruction was proper.

issues.label: Flight instruction propriety
issues.why: If given, the court must ensure evidence supports inferences of flight, consciousness of guilt, and relation to charged offenses.

issues.label: CSLI acquisition legality
issues.why: The court must determine whether historical CSLI was obtained with a warrant or lawful process under Carpenter and local law.

issues.label: CSLI admissibility and foundation
issues.why: The court must confirm proper authentication, explanation of methodology, and limits of location inference for tower data.

issues.label: Expert testimony on CSLI
issues.why: If CSLI interpretation required expertise, the court must decide whether qualified expert testimony was necessary and properly admitted.

issues.label: Fourth Amendment suppression issues
issues.why: Any unlawful search/seizure (CSLI, car location, tarp/garage observation) requires analysis of suppression and good-faith exceptions.

issues.label: Plain-view/curtilage garage issues
issues.why: Observing a tarp-covered Maserati in a garage may implicate curtilage and consent; the court must evaluate legality if challenged.

issues.label: Discovery compliance (Brady/Giglio)
issues.why: The court must ensure the government disclosed material exculpatory or impeachment evidence (e.g., Johnson’s undisclosed interaction detail).

issues.label: Late disclosure remedies
issues.why: If disclosure was delayed, the court must assess prejudice and whether continuance, exclusion, or mistrial was required.

issues.label: Witness credibility/impeachment limits
issues.why: The court must assess whether the defense was improperly limited in cross-examining key witnesses (Confrontation Clause).

issues.label: Admission of victim injuries evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether medical testimony/photos/fragments were relevant and not unfairly prejudicial.

issues.label: Chain of custody for fragments
issues.why: If physical evidence was introduced, the court must ensure sufficient chain-of-custody showing.

issues.label: Intent for AWIKWA
issues.why: AWIKWA requires specific intent to kill; the court must determine whether evidence supports that mental state.

issues.label: AWIKWA while armed elements
issues.why: The court must confirm proof of assault, intent to kill, and being armed with a dangerous weapon.

issues.label: ADW elements for each victim
issues.why: For each ADW count, the court must confirm an assault with a dangerous weapon and requisite intent/apprehension as defined by D.C. law.

issues.label: ADW against uninjured child
issues.why: For P.N. (uninjured), the court must assess whether evidence shows the child was assaulted (attempted battery or threatened with ability).

issues.label: ADW against child with glass injury
issues.why: For A.S., the court must assess causation and whether the assault was by gunfire and dangerous weapon, not merely accident after crash.

issues.label: ADW victim in car behind
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether shots “in the direction” of trailing cars created an assault against a specific person and met intent/ability requirements.

issues.label: Specificity of assault victim
issues.why: The court must determine whether the government proved the named victim was the person assaulted rather than an undifferentiated crowd.

issues.label: Transferred intent applicability
issues.why: If defendant aimed at Nance but endangered others, the court must consider whether transferred intent supports ADW counts.

issues.label: Unit of prosecution for assaults
issues.why: The court must ensure multiple assault convictions correspond to distinct victims and are not multiplicitous.

issues.label: PFCOV predicate validity
issues.why: Each PFCOV count requires a qualifying crime of violence; the court must confirm predicates (AWIKWA/ADW) qualify.

issues.label: PFCOV evidence sufficiency
issues.why: The court must decide whether firearm possession/use during each predicate offense was proved beyond a reasonable doubt.

issues.label: Multiplicity of PFCOV counts
issues.why: The court must determine whether multiple PFCOV counts for a single shooting episode are permissible or must merge.

issues.label: Merger of PFCOV at sentencing
issues.why: Even if convictions stand, the court must verify the correctness of merging PFCOV convictions and imposing a single sentence.

issues.label: Double jeopardy/merger AWIKWA-ADW
issues.why: The court must assess whether any ADW merges into AWIKWA as lesser-included for the same victim (Nance) or whether counts are distinct.

issues.label: Consistency of verdicts
issues.why: The court must address any claim that verdicts are legally inconsistent and whether that matters under D.C. law.

issues.label: Prosecutorial misconduct in argument
issues.why: If raised, the court must review whether closing arguments improperly vouched, misstated evidence, or inflamed passions.

issues.label: Admission of press release evidence
issues.why: If referenced at trial, the court must decide whether the June 2 press release was admissible or prejudicial.

issues.label: Right to present a defense
issues.why: Any exclusion of defense evidence (alternative suspect, misidentification, etc.) must be evaluated under due process and evidentiary rules.

issues.label: Jury unanimity requirements
issues.why: The court must ensure jurors were required to be unanimous as to each count and, if multiple acts supported a count, on the act theory if required.

issues.label: Lesser-included offense instructions
issues.why: If requested, the court must decide whether lesser-included instructions (e.g., ADW/assault) were warranted and properly handled.

issues.label: Sentencing legality under D.C. Code
issues.why: The court must verify each sentence falls within statutory ranges and mandatory minimums/maximums.

issues.label: Consecutive vs concurrent authority
issues.why: The court must determine whether the court had authority to run AWIKWA and ADW sentences consecutively and whether it exercised discretion properly.

issues.label: Sentencing explanation adequacy
issues.why: The court must confirm the judge provided a reasoned basis for the sentence and addressed required factors.

issues.label: Consideration of mitigating evidence
issues.why: The court must ensure the court considered relevant mitigation (history, lack of record, etc.) and did not rely on improper factors.

issues.label: Vindictive sentencing concerns
issues.why: The court must ensure the sentence was not imposed to punish the defendant for going to trial or exercising rights.

issues.label: Proportionality/Eighth Amendment
issues.why: A 32.5-year aggregate sentence may raise proportionality concerns that must be assessed if argued.

issues.label: Apprendi/Blakely facts at sentencing
issues.why: The court must ensure any fact increasing statutory maximum/minimum was found by the jury or admitted, not solely by the judge.

issues.label: Correctness of merging convictions
issues.why: Beyond PFCOV, the court must ensure any other counts that should merge were properly merged and not separately punished.

issues.label: Credit for time served and custody
issues.why: If disputed, the court must ensure lawful calculation of jail credit and commencement of sentences.

issues.label: Restitution/fees/orders legality
issues.why: If imposed, the court must confirm any restitution or assessments were authorized and supported by findings.

issues.label: Competency to stand trial
issues.why: If any record indication exists, the court must ensure the defendant was competent throughout proceedings.

issues.label: Effective assistance of counsel
issues.why: If raised or apparent, the court must address whether counsel’s performance was deficient and prejudicial, or defer to collateral review as appropriate.

issues.label: Record completeness for review
issues.why: The court must ensure transcripts/exhibits are sufficient to resolve claims or order reconstruction/remand if missing.
